_comment: Stage goals, the 3-star formula and the bridge-keeper quizzes for Stages 1 to 5 (FR-EVA-001, FR-EVA-002). Tuning a stage means editing this file, not GDScript. Objective types are counted by StageSession from FarmEvents: plant, water, harvest, collect_crop, till, sell_earned, buy_supply, treat_pest, grade_a, plant_tree, collect_fruit, chop_tree, harvest_seasons, sow_in_season.

evaluation._comment: score = time * weight_time + crops * weight_crops + quiz * weight_quiz. Each part is 0..1. time = par / actual (capped at 1), crops = harvested / target (capped at 1), quiz = correct / asked on the winning attempt. The bridge opens once every objective is done, which is what earns the first star.

keeper.name: Keeper Thandi
keeper.intro: Hold it! Nobody crosses my bridge without showing they know the basics.
keeper.win: Well grown! The market island is all yours.
keeper.lose: Not yet. Go look after a few more crops and come back.

questions.q: The soil around your seedling dries out. What does that cost you?
questions.explain: Dry soil stresses the plant, and every stressed day takes weight off the harvest.

questions.q: What must you do to grass before you can sow seed in it?
questions.explain: Seed needs loose, turned soil. The hoe opens a bed you can plant in.

questions.q: When is a cabbage ready to cut?
questions.explain: Cut when the head is firm. Left standing too long, cabbage heads split.

questions.q: Can you give a crop too much water?
options: Yes, soaked soil damages the roots
questions.explain: Waterlogged soil starves roots of air. Aim for moist, not soaked.

keeper.name: Keeper Bongani
keeper.intro: A farm is a business too. Let's see if you can count your rand.
keeper.win: Sharp! You'll need that head for numbers where pests live.
keeper.lose: Check the market prices again, then try me once more.

questions.q: Cabbage seed costs R9 and the harvest sells for R64. What is your profit on one plant?
questions.explain: Profit is what you earn minus what you spent: R64 - R9 = R55.

questions.q: What does a bag of fertiliser do for a crop you sow?
options: Grows faster and starts in damper soil
questions.explain: Fertiliser speeds development and gives the seedling moister soil to start in.

questions.q: What decides how much money a harvest brings in?
options: The time of day you sell
questions.explain: The market pays per kilogram, and Grade A pays more than Grade B.

questions.q: You have R20. Maize seed costs R18 and cabbage seed costs R9. What can you afford to sow?
questions.explain: Two cabbage cost R18. Two maize (R36) or maize plus cabbage (R27) are over budget.

keeper.name: Keeper Lerato
keeper.intro: Pests don't wait for you, and neither do I. Answer quickly!
keeper.win: Your crops are in good hands. The orchard is next.
keeper.lose: The bugs won that round. Watch your plants closely and return.

questions.q: A caterpillar is sitting on your cabbage. What should you do?
options: Treat it as soon as you can
questions.explain: Every day a pest feeds untreated takes weight off the crop.

questions.q: What happens if you use a treatment on a healthy plant?
questions.explain: Treat only what is infested. A spray on a clean plant is a purchase thrown away.

questions.q: Pests fed on a crop for days before you cleared them. How will it most likely sell?
options: Grade B, the lost weight stays lost
questions.explain: Health can recover, but the damage already done is permanent and lowers the grade.

questions.q: Birds keep landing on your crops. Which control works on them?
questions.explain: Insecticide is for insects. Birds are scared off, which the organic kit's scare tape does.

keeper.name: Keeper Pieter
keeper.intro: Trees take patience. Let's see if you have some.
keeper.win: A true orchard keeper. The seasons are waiting for you.
keeper.lose: Spend a little more time among the trees, then come back.

questions.q: How do you get the fruit off a mature, fruiting tree?
questions.explain: Shaking brings the fruit down and leaves the tree standing to fruit again.

questions.q: You have just picked a tree clean. What happens next?
options: It regrows fruit after a few days
questions.explain: Fruit trees are perennial. Picked trees grow fresh fruit after a few days.

questions.q: Why chop down an old tree that no longer fruits?
options: For timber and to free up space
questions.explain: Old timber is useful and clearing it makes room for young, productive trees.

questions.q: You plant a sapling today. When will it bear fruit?
options: Once it has grown through its stages over several days
questions.explain: A sapling grows through young and growing stages before it is mature enough to fruit.

objectives.label: Sow 3 crops that suit the season

keeper.name: Keeper Nomsa
keeper.intro: Every season has its crop. Show me you know which is which.
keeper.win: You read the seasons like a real farmer. Well done!
keeper.lose: The weather got the better of you. Watch the calendar and try again.

questions.q: Maize needs at least 10 degrees to grow. Winter here is 6 degrees. What happens to maize sown in winter?
questions.explain: Below its minimum growth temperature a crop simply stops developing.

questions.q: In which season does the soil dry out fastest?
questions.explain: Summer heat makes soil lose water about half again as fast, so water more often.

questions.q: Which crop still does well in autumn?
questions.explain: Cabbage is a cool-season crop. Maize slows to a crawl as it cools down.

questions.q: A warning says winter is coming. What is the best move?
options: Harvest what is standing before it arrives
questions.explain: Nothing develops in winter, so bring in ready crops before the cold stalls them.
